premise: At 58, after 26 years as a school cafeteria monitor, I returned to care for my dying father, who left me 60% of his 1950s roller-skating rink and retro arcade worth $590,000, but my half-brother forged a codicil cutting me out and sold the rink to a trampoline-park chain for $840,000, mailing me a $4,500 'skate lace' check. I found Dad's original will sealed inside a hollow rental-skate boot in the lost-and-found bin, voided the sale, and now run 'Skate of Deceit Roller Rink,' where he polishes rental skates in a smock that says 'Skated My Inheritance' and every admission ticket prints his probate-fraud docket.
